newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Banco Totta stocks slide in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Banco Totta stocks slide in heavy trade.

text.p: Shares in Banco Totta & Acores (BTA) slid 3.5 percent to 2,760 escudos, with apparently one large sell order from abroad pressuring the stock, trader said.
They said the weakness was motivated by what were being seen as disappointing nine month results and manoeuvering ahead of the final phase of the bank's privatisation this month.
"There was a big sale order, I think from abroad. It must have to do with the nine month results and the privatisation," one trader said.

Traders said that closer study of the nine month figures, in which the bank posted a 5.7 percent rise in net profit year-on-year, showed that the advance had been secured through a fall in provisions rather than an significant business improvement.
But they said that the pressure on the price was also linked to the fact that the bulk of the 13.2 percent of Banco Totta that the government is selling will be placed through direct sale.
"There must be some people who believe the privatisation price will be lower and that therefore they can buy back more cheaply," said another trader.
